title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: how many originals an issuance puts into circulation
content:
## Scope

This rule of the Bills of Lading and Transport Documents product fixes the number of originals of the set in force put into circulation when an approved transport document is issued.

## Formal clause

1. The number put into circulation is the tier's number of originals issued per set when the document's status is approved at the moment of issue and the booking the document covers counts as on board under its recorded status.
2. On a tier whose number of originals issued per set is zero, no originals exist.
3. When the document is in any other status, or the booking status does not count as on board, no originals are put into circulation and the number is zero.
4. A zero never permits issuing a document whose cargo has not been shipped, which the product's issuance rules forbid; it only records that no originals would go into circulation.
5. The prepaid-freight hold of the issuance rules decides whether the document may be issued at all, and does not change the number.
6. The number is a whole number of original documents.

## Truth table

| Document approved at the moment of issue | Booking counts as on board | Originals put into circulation |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Tier's originals issued per set (none on a tier whose figure is zero) |
| Yes | No | Zero |
| No | Yes | Zero |
| No | No | Zero |

## Hypothetical illustration

For illustration only, take a tier with a hypothetical figure of 2 originals per set. An approved document with a qualifying booking puts 2 originals into circulation at issue. The same document with a booking that does not qualify gives zero, and that zero does not make the issuance permissible.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** when prepaid freight is still unpaid, the document is issued with fewer originals. **Correct basis:** the prepaid-freight hold only decides whether the document may be issued at all; it never changes the number of originals.
- **Wrong reading:** a zero allows a document to be issued before the cargo is on board. **Correct basis:** the zero only records that no originals go into circulation; issuing before shipment stays forbidden.
